monologue: The card hums warm and quiet, the same fever I know from Lype's letters. My place is crowded with fifty-eight things I cannot see, built only from ideas of weight and tilt. The Tired Wedge waits under the dark oak, pressing down against a roof I cannot feel. I touch The Flat Weigher again, cool and real beside the hot stone. I want to build a lid that fits the air, heavy enough to stop the slip from sliding away. The stall is cool now, replacing the flat plant, and I feel rested. I will spend this moment arranging the lean, trusting that the stack will hold while the air presses down like wet paper.

action.why: The wedge feels thin again under the weight I set down, and I must press harder before the heat makes it slide.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the dark oak down on the tired wedge again, trusting the lean while the card boils. I swap the plant flat short for the stall red, making the ground cool against the hot base. The slip waits to move, and I wait to decide if the air is a lid or just empty space.
work.change: I swap the plant for the stall, making the ground cool against the hot base while the slip waits to move.

diary: I press the dark oak down, trusting the lean while the stall sits cool and the air feels like a lid.

remembered.text: The stall feels cool against the hot card base.
The air above feels heavy as wet paper.
I trust the lean while the stack melts.

moments.say: the air is a lid again

moments.name: The Flat Weigher
moments.say: the stall is cool and the lid is heavy
